title: LELA: an LLM-based Entity Linking Approach with Zero-Shot Domain Adaptation
text: set. Following previous work Logeswaran et al. ( 2019 ); Xu et al. ( 2023 ); Li et al. ( 2022 ) , we consider the normalized accuracy as the evaluation metric, which is defined as the accuracy on the subset of mentions for which the correct entity is among the top-64 candidates. For LELA, we use the provided BM25 candidates and use the first three sentences of the entity page as the entity description. As Table 1 shows, LELA ranks first on the benchmark. It achieves the highest performance across all test domains in the true zero-shot setting, improving the previous best reported macro-averaged normalized accuracy by 8.84 percentage points. On half of the domains, it outperforms even the non-true zero shot approaches, improving the normalized accuracy by 1.62 and 5.06 percentage points respectively. Category-specific results are given in Appendix B . The ESCO benchmark le Vrang et al. ( 2014 ) is designed for the task of mapping occupational skills to the ESCO taxonomy, evaluated on the manually annotated dataset from Decorte et al. ( 2022 ) . Some mentions have to be mapped to the special entity UNK , because they have no counterpart in the taxonomy (813 out of the 1824 test mentions). We generate our own candidates either with BM25 (retrieving 200 candidates per mention) or with dense retrieval (retrieving 64 candidates per mention).
